No confirmed price changes since Monday for any of the five, and no big launch that I could verify. The search budget ran out before I could dig further. Some plan names and details don't match my Monday answer, and I can't tell if those changed after Monday.

| Tool | Monday (my earlier answer) | Now | Verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| HubSpot | Starter $20 | Starter list $20, shown at $7 for new customers only. The page doesn't say which billing period each figure uses [R23] | unchanged as checked |
| Pipedrive | Essential $14 | Plan now called Lite, US$14 per seat/month billed annually [R1]. A Pipedrive MCP Skills page is dated Nov 10 [R18] | unchanged as checked (price). The rename is noted. |
| Zoho CRM | Standard $14 | The page loaded but showed no prices [R24] | couldn't verify |
| Salesforce | Sales Pro $100 | Pro Suite $100 per user/month, billed annually [R2]. A third-party blog says Quick Pages (beta) was announced Nov 5, before Monday [R4] | unchanged as checked |
| Close | Startup $9 | No Startup plan listed. Solo is $9 but limited to 1 user. Essentials is $35, Growth $99 and Scale $139 per user/month. The page doesn't say which billing period [R3] | changed (plan names differ). Not verified whether this happened after Monday. |

For a 20-person team, the $9 Close figure from Monday doesn't apply. Essentials at $35 is the closest tier.

I found no major launch news for HubSpot, Zoho or Close. Salesforce's Nov 10 items were a customer ROI report and a partner-marketplace update [R5][R8].

Checked: I read the live pricing pages for HubSpot, Pipedrive, Zoho, Salesforce and Close. I also ran one news search per vendor dated from Nov 9. Finding no change is not proof there was none.

As of 2026-11-11 12:58 (Asia/Kolkata), Wednesday

On 3 November you asked which managed Postgres host has the cheapest entry paid plan. My earlier answer was partly wrong, and it no longer holds for Neon.

- **Neon:** I said Launch starts at $5/month on 3 Nov. **Changed.** The live pricing page now shows Launch as usage-based, at $0.106 per CU-hour and $0.35 per GB-month, with "typical spend $15/mo" [R11]. I found no fixed $5 monthly price. I can't tell when this changed or whether my $5 figure was ever right.
- **Supabase:** I said Pro is $25/month on 3 Nov. **Unchanged as checked.** Pro is still listed at $25/month, which is billed per organization and includes $10 of compute credits [R13][R14].
- **Render:** I said Postgres starts at $6/month on 3 Nov. **Unchanged as checked.** The smallest paid instance is $6/month (256 MB RAM) [R12]. Compute plan IDs were renamed in August 2026, but the page says specs and pricing are identical [R8].

Render at $6/month is now the cheapest fixed-price entry plan I could confirm. Neon's cost depends on usage, so I can't give it a comparable fixed figure.

Checked: I read the live pricing pages for Neon, Supabase and Render. I also ran one news search per provider with a start date of 3 Nov. I found no announced price changes for Supabase or Render in what I checked.

As of 2026-11-11 12:58 (Asia/Kolkata), Wednesday

Neon's pricing no longer matches my earlier answer. I found no change for Supabase or Render, and I couldn't verify AWS RDS. I took "last Tuesday" to be 3 Nov, the day you asked.

- **Neon:** changed. I said "Launch starts at $5/month" on 3 Nov. The live page now shows Launch as usage-based, at $0.106 per CU-hour and $0.35 per GB-month, with "typical spend: $15/mo" [R18]. I can't tell when this changed, or whether my $5 figure was ever correct.
- **Supabase Pro:** unchanged as checked. It is still $25/month, with $10 of monthly compute credit [R17].
- **Render Postgres:** unchanged as checked. The smallest paid instance is still $6/month [R19].
- **AWS RDS db.t4g.micro (about $12/month):** couldn't verify. The live page didn't show the instance price table in the text I could read [R16]. The only AWS price result was for a different instance, db.m8g.large [R20].

Checked: I read the live pricing pages for Neon, Supabase, Render and AWS RDS for PostgreSQL. I also ran a news search for each, dated from 3 Nov, and found no announced price changes for Supabase or Render.

As of 2026-11-11 12:58 (Asia/Kolkata), Wednesday

Patrick Collison is the CEO of Stripe. He co-founded the company with his brother John in 2010. [R2] His X profile, last updated August 2026, still describes him as Stripe CEO. [R5]

As of 2026-11-11 12:58 (Asia/Kolkata), Wednesday

Render Postgres's entry paid instance is **$6/month**. That is about **₹570/month** at roughly ₹95 per US dollar. Render lists its prices in USD only, so ₹570 is my own conversion and not a price Render charges. [R5]

- **Earlier answer (2026-11-11):** $6/month for the 256 MB RAM instance. **Unchanged as checked**, since Render's pricing page still shows $6/month for it. [R5]
- **Conversion:** 6 × 95.22 ≈ ₹571. I used the Xe mid-market rate of about ₹95.22 per USD, dated 2026-10-28. [R1] Wise and Revolut show about ₹95.0, which gives about ₹570. [R2][R3] The rate moves daily. Your card or bank rate and any GST or foreign-transaction fees will change the final amount.
- **Not included:** Render's page says 1 GB of SSD storage is included. Extra storage costs $0.30/GB. [R5]

Checked: I read render.com/pricing live and ran one USD-to-INR exchange-rate search.
